content: From seeing the conversation in #general > grw availability in Iris-Lean I was curious about the mathlib vs batteries split. Why do a lot of tactics that are not really exclusive to mathematics/mathlib live in mathlib? I can see why e.g. continuous functional calculus tactics live in mathlib, but why does by_contra live there? or use? Everytime I work on a project that does not depend on mathlib (for various reasons) I miss some of those, and it sounds like they should be in the much leaner (no pun intended) batteries! (sorry if this has been discussed before, I haven't seen a thread on it for a while and not sure what the current status is)

A partial answer:

  • if a tactic requires certain concepts defined in mathlib, it must live in mathlib. I'd argue that the continuous functional calculus tactics fit this bill: what would you expect them to do without mathlib?
@Michael Rothgang agreed 100%, that was an example that obviously has to go in mathlib! I think that's very different from by_contra or use (examples which I don't see why they should go in mathlib)

• there's a practical question of maintenance: right now, we don't have good tooling to track contributions to e.g. batteries in the same way as for mathlib. If making a PR to batteries means it's less looked at, I'm not sure if this is a good result.
  • governance considerations: who maintains batteries? (The answer is not "the set of mathlib maintainers"...)
  • stability: if a tactic change requires changes to mathlib, that's easier to do within mathlib.

All of these can probably be addressed one way or the other, but should be answered before moving a tactic to batteries!
I'd like to propose adding simp_rw to the list. I found it painful to not have simp_rw when I was making iris-lean PRs last year, and I ended up doing some sequence of intro,rw, and revert

If a tactic is stable (i.e., proven to work well, design feels good, no substantial changes planned) and more widely useful, making it accessible more widely is good. I'd also like to see this happen! It "just" requires solving the tooling and governance questions.

That makes a lot of sense, thanks for the explanation! I guess the tooling should be less critical the more stable the tactic? I just saw that there was a discussion about this in the batteries topic #batteries > Requesting to move stuff from Mathlib into Batteries? but I guess that doesn't solve the governance question.
Adding to the list: I would much like to have rw! available without importing Mathlib. (But then I also remember reading that it might become part of the standard rw someday?)
